sources.text:
Dva tankera za naftu pod indijskom zastavom prošla su danas kroz Hormuški moreuz u ponedjeljak, saopštilo je indijsko Ministarstvo pomorskog saobraćaja.
Očekuje se da će brodovi „Jag-Vasant“ i „Pine-Gas“, koji prevoze ukupno 92.000 tona tečnog naftnog gasa (TNG), stići u indijske luke između 26. i 28. marta, navelo je ministarstvo.
Dva druga broda sa TNG-om pod indijskom zastavom prethodno su prošla kroz Hormuški moreuz.
Indijski premijer Narendra Modi rekao je danas da je Indija u bliskom kontaktu sa svojim saveznicima kako bi zaštitila lance snabdijevanja pogođene ratom.
Nju Delhi održava dobre odnose sa Teheranom, ali je značajno ojačao saradnju sa Izraelom u oblastima odbrane, poljoprivrede, tehnologije i sajber bezbjednosti, prenio je pariski list „Mond“ (Le Monde) na svom sajtu.
„Radimo na tome da brodovi koji prevoze naftu, gas, đubriva i drugu neophodnu robu bezbjedno stignu do Indije“, rekao je Modi u parlamentu.
Prema njegovim riječima, Indija se protivi napadima na civilnu infrastrukturu za transport energije.
„Napadi na trgovačke brodove i plovne puteve poput Hormuškog moreuza su neprihvatljivi“, dodao je indijski premijer.
(BETA)
Islamabad je "već spreman da bude domaćin razgovora" u koje bi bili uključeni Iran, Sjedinjene Američke Države i Izrael, rekao je portparol pakistanskog Ministarstva spoljnih poslova CNN‑u, samo o nekoliksati nakon što je Teheran odbacio tvrdnje da su SAD i Iran preko vikenda otvorili diplomatski kanal za pregovore.
"Ako se obje strane slože, Pakistan je uvijek spreman da ugosti razgovore", rekao je portparol Ministarstva spoljnih poslova Tahir Husajn Andrabi.
Pakistan je, kako su regionalni izvori ranije navodili, aktivno angažovan u diplomatskim naporima da posreduje između Vašingtona i Teherana i potencijalno pomogne u smanjenju tenzija u regionu.
Premijer Izraela Benjamin Netanjahu izjavio je da je razgovarao s Donaldom Trumpom, te da vidi mogućnost postizanja dogovora s Iranom, prenosi Gardijan.
Tamp vjerujeoda postoji mogućnost "iskorištavanja moćnih postignuća Izraelskih odbrambenih snaga i američke vojske, kako bi se ostvarili ciljevi rata kroz dogovor - dogovor koji će očuvati naše vitalne interese", tvrdi Netanjahu u video izjavi koju je objavila njegova kancelarija.
On je ipak istakao da će Izrael nastaviti svoje napade protiv Irana i Libana.
"Mi ćemo štititi naše vitalne interese pod svim okolnostima. Istovremeno, nastavljamo da udaramo i u Iranu i u Libanu", kazao je.
Portparol iranske vojske izjavio je da Iran ima potpunu kontrolu nad regionom Perzijskog zaliva, Hormuškim moreuzom i vodama uz Oman, tvrdeći da Teheranu nije potrebno da postavlja mine u zalivu da bi potvrđivao svoj položaj.
"Islamska Republika Iran ima punu i snažnu kontrolu nad regionom Perzijskog zaliva, teritorijalnim vodama Omana i Hormuškim moreuzom. Stoga, zbog dovoljno nadmoćnog položaja i moći, neće biti potrebe za postavljanjem mina u Perzijskom zalivu, i koristićemo sva moguća sredstva da osiguramo bezbjednost po potrebi", rekao je portparol, prenijeli su iranski mediji.
Zvaničnik je rekao da iranske oružane snage mogu obezbijediti bezbjednost u Perzijskom zalivu i upozorio da zemlje izvan regiona nemaju pravo da se miješaju u ovu oblast.
Govoreći u Memfisu, Donald Tramp je ponovo iznio tvrdnju da Teheran želi da postigne dogovor i da postoji veoma dobra šansa da se postigne sporazum s Iranom, prenosi Gardijan.
"Eliminisali smo sve što se može eliminisati u Iranu, uključujući lidere", rekao je on.
Teheran ima još jednu priliku da okonča svoje prijetnje prema Sjedinjenim Američkim Državama i njihovim saveznicima, dodao je Tramp.
"Sada vodimo zaista dobre razgovore. Počeli su sinoć, malo i noć prije toga. Mislim da su veoma dobri. Žele mir. Saglasili su se da neće imati nuklearno oružje. Ali vidjećemo. Moramo da to završimo", naveo je on.
Iranska agencija Fars prenosi, pozivajući se na izvore koje opisuje kao upućene, da se pripremaju planovi za potencijalne akcije usmjerene na Tel Aviv i neke regionalne saveznike SAD i Izraela.
"Specijalni planovi su pripremljeni večeras za Tel Aviv i neke regionalne saveznike SAD i Izraela, što će potpuno ukloniti svaku nadu u pregovore iz uma agresora", prenio je Fars, agencija povezana s Iranskom revolucionarnom gardom.
Izraelska vojska saopštila je da je danas pogodila jednu od glavnih baza Iranske revolucionarne garde, zajedno sa nekoliko drugih vojnih objekata u glavnom gradu Teheranu, prenosi Gardijan.
Izraelsko ratno vazduhoplovstvo izvelo je široku seriju udara na infrastrukturu iranskog režima, navode Izraelske odbrambene snage (IDF) u saopštenju.
Ranije danas, iranska novinska agencija Fars prenijela je da je u izraelskim udarima pogođeno više lokacija širom Teherana. U međuvremenu, iranski Crveni polumjesec saopštio je da traži jedno dijete ispod ruševina stambene zgrade u Teheranu.
IDF je naveo da su među ciljevima bila sjedišta iranskih bezbjednosnih organizacija i ključna mjesta za proizvodnju oružja, kao i dodatni objekti za proizvodnju i istraživački centri vezani za elektroniku, balističke projektile i bojeve glave.
Predsjednik iranskog parlamenta Mohamed Bager Galibaf, izjavio je da nisu vođeni nikakvi pregovori sa Sjedinjenim Američkim Državama nakon što je predsjednik SAD Donald Tramp najavio da se razgovori nastavljaju, prenosi CNN.
"Nisu vođeni nikakvi pregovori sa SAD, a lažne vijesti se koriste za manipulaciju finansijskim i naftnim tržištima i za izbjegavanje ćorsokaka u kojem su SAD i Izrael zarobljeni,“ naveo je Galibaf u objavi na Iksu.
Negova izjava je uslijedila nakon što je Tramp ranije danas kazao da je imao vrlo dobre razgovore sa neimenovanim iranskim zvaničnikom, nakon što je naglo odložio planove za napad na iranske elektrane.
Novinska agencija Aksios, pozivajući se na neimenovanog izraelskog zvaničnika, navela je da je Trampov sagovornik bio Galibaf.
Portparol iranskog Ministarstva vanjskih poslova, Esmail Bakei, rekao je da su primljene poruke od "nekih prijateljskih zemalja koje ukazuju na američki zahtjev za pregovorima s ciljem okončanja rata", prenijela je zvanična iranska agencija IRNA.
U Bahreinu je odjeknulo nekoliko snažnih eksplozija i oglasile su se sirene za vazdušnu uzbunu, javlja novinar agencije AFP, prvi put u Zalivu otkako je američki predsjednik Donald Tramp najavio da su u toku razgovori o okončanju rata s Iranom.
"Građani i stanovnici se pozivaju da ostanu mirni i da se upute ka najbližem sigurnom mjestu“, saopštilo je Ministarstvo unutrašnjih poslova Bahreina na društvenim mrežama.
Izraelske vlasti su uspjele da preotmu kontrolu nad uličnim nadzornim kamerama u Iranu i iskoriste ih u operacijama ubijanja najviših predstavnika te države, što je sredstvo koje se sve češće koristi u modernim ratovima.
Nedavni napredak u vještačkoj inteligenciji omogućio je vojsci i obavještajnim agencijama da pregledaju ogromne količine snimaka nadzornih kamera i identifikuju mete.
Potencijal takvih sistema da budu hakovani i korišćeni protiv protivnika Izrael je demonstrirao 28. februara, kada je pratio vrhovnog vođu Irana ajatolaha Alija Hamneija uz pomoć uličnih kamera u Teheranu, prema poznavaocima i analizama procurelih podataka, javnih izjava i izvještaja Asošiejted presa.
Američki ministar energetike Kris Rajt izjavio je danas da su poremećaji na tržištu nafte povezani sa ratom na Bliskom istoku „privremeni“.
Govoreći na konferenciji o energetskom sektoru u američkoj saveznoj državi Teksas, Rajt je rekao da cijene još nijesu dostigle nivo dovoljno visok da izazovu značajan pad potražnje.
Rajt je dodao da američka administracija preduzima „pragmatične korake“ kako bi povećala raspoloživu ponudu.
Kao dio napora koje koordinira Međunarodna agencija za energiju, Sjedinjene Američke Države su u petak počele da puštaju dio svojih strateških rezervi na tržište.
Količina puštena do sada „trebalo bi da predstavlja otprilike tri miliona barela“ od više od 415 miliona koliko je dostupno Sjedinjenim Američkim Državama, rekao je Rajt i dodao da će zemlja obnoviti svoje rezerve do kraja 2027. godine.
(BETA)
Ukrajinska vojna obavještajna služba posjeduje neoborive dokaze da Rusija nastavlja da pruža obavještajne podatke Iranu, izjavio je ukrajinski predsjednik Volodimir Zelenski, nakon sastanka sa šefom vojne obavještajne službe, prenosi Gardijan.
"Rusija koristi sopstvene kapacitete za elektronsko izviđanje i izviđanje signala, kao i dio podataka dobijenih kroz saradnju sa partnerima na Bliskom istoku", rekao je on u objavi na Iksu..
Kremlj je prošle sedmice odbacio izvještaj Vol strit žurnala da Rusija dijeli satelitske snimke i unaprijeđenu tehnologiju dronova s Iranom, nazivajući ga lažnim vijestima.
Sjedinjene Američke Države zatražile su sastanak sa predsjednikom iranskog parlamenta Mohamedom Bagerom Kalibafom u subotu, rekao je visoki iranski zvaničnik agenciji Rojters, ne navodeći mjesto predloženog susreta.
Zvaničnik, koji je tražio da ostane anoniman zbog osjetljivosti pitanja, rekao je da Vrhovno vijeće za nacionalnu bezbjednost SAD još nije donijelo odluku o predloženim razgovorima i da Iran još nije odgovorio, prenosi Gardijan.
Portparol iranskog Ministarstva vanjskih poslova negirao je da su u posljednja 24 dana vođeni bilo kakvi razgovori sa Sjedinjenim Američkim Državama, čime je ozbiljno podrio tvrdnje Donalda Trampa da su SAD i Iran imali "veoma dobre i produktivne razgovore“ o okončanju rata, prenosi Gardijan.
Posljednjih dana "prijateljske zemlje" su prenosile poruke da su SAD zatražile razgovore radi završetka rata, a Iran je odgovorio "na odgovarajući način" u skladu sa "principijelnim stavovima zemlje". prenijela je državna novinska agencija IRNA izjavu portparola ministarstva Esmaila Bagaija.
On je dodao je da bi svaka akcija protiv iranske energetske infrastrukture naišla na "odlučan, trenutni i efektivan" odgovor iranskih oružanih snaga, te istaka da se iranski stav o Hormuškom moreuzu i uslovima za okončanje rata nisu promijenili.
Britanski premijer Kir Starmer izjavio je da Velika Britanija mora da planira mogućnost da rat na Bliskom istoku potraje "izvjesno vrijeme" i upozorio da ne treba gajiti lažni osjećaj sigurnosti da bi sukob mogao brzo da se završi, prenosi Gardijan.
Odgovarajući na pitanje parlamentarnog odbora da li London smatra da bi rat mogao trajati mjesecima, a ne danima ili sedmicama, Starmer je rekao: "Moramo planirati na osnovu pretpostavke da bi to moglo da traje neko vrijeme".
On je dodao da su svi napori Velike Britanije usmjereni ka brzom smirivanju sukoba.
Od početka rata prošlog mjeseca, Starmer je, kako kaže, poručio svom timu da ne smiju upasti u zamku lažnog uvjerenja da će ovo nužno imati brz završetak.
Predsjednik SAD Donald Tramp rekao je za CNN da će Hormuški moreuz biti otvoren vrlo brzo, dodajući da bi volio da ta ključna pomorska ruta bude pod zajedničkom kontrolom Sjedinjenih Američkih Država i Irana.
Na pitanje novinarke CNN-a Kejtlin Kolins kada se može očekivati ponovno otvaranje moreuza, Tramp je odgovorio: "Biće otvoren vrlo brzo", ukoliko pregovori s Iranom budu tekli planiranom dinamikom.
"Biće pod zajedničkom kontrolom. Ja i ajatolah, ko god da je ajatolah, odnosno ko god bude sljedeći ajatolah", dodao je Tramp.
"A doći će i do veoma ozbiljne promjene režima“, rekao je predsjednik SAD, pozivajući se na napade u ranoj fazi sukoba u kojima je eliminisan veliki dio iranskog vojnog i političkog vrha.
"To automatski znači promjenu režima“, dodao je, uz ocjenu da su razgovori tokom vikenda pokazali mogućnost smirivanja sukoba.
"Ali razgovaramo s ljudima koje smatram veoma razumnim i pouzdanim. Ljudi unutar sistema znaju ko su oni, veoma su poštovani i možda će neko od njih biti upravo ono što tražimo", rekao je Tramp.
Predsjednik Donald Tramp nagovijestio je da će i dalje tražiti 200 milijardi dolara za Pentagon, iako je najavio da namjerava da okonča rat s Iranom.
"Dobro je imati finansije, uvijek je dobro imati, svijet je veoma zapaljiv. A demokrate ga dodatno raspiruju, znate, uglavnom demokrate", rekao je Tramp za CNN u Vest Palm Biču na Floridi.
CNN je objavio da bi Tramp u narednim sedmicama mogao zatražiti od Kongresa da mu odobri i do 200 milijardi dolara za finansiranje tekućeg rata.
Dva muškarca povrijeđena su od gelera nakon što su rakete ispaljene prema izraelskom gradu Kirjat Šmona, koji se nalazi blizu granice s Libanom, saopštile su danas službe za hitne intervencije.
Napad je uslijedio nakon što je tokom vikenda na desetine Izraelaca ranjeno u iranskom raketnom udaru.
Jedan muškarac je u teškom stanju s povredom glave i helikopterom je prebačen u bolnicu, saopštila je izraelska služba za hitne slučajeve Magen David Adom. Drugi muškarac je lakše povrijeđen.
Prema navodima lokalnih vlasti, muškarci su povrijeđeni na dvije različite lokacije udara.
Više država posljednjih dana prenosi poruke između Sjedinjenih Američkih Država i Irana u pokušaju da se smanje rastuće tenzije oko energetskih postrojenja i elektrana, navode za CNN izvori upoznati s razgovorima.
Turska i Egipat su, prema tim izvorima, prenijeli određene poruke u okviru tih napora. Istovremeno, izaslanik predsjednika Donalda Trampa za vanjsku politiku Stiv Vitkof dobio je upozorenja od više regionalnih zvaničnika da bi Trampova prijetnja napadima na iranske elektrane izazvala snažan odgovor, uključujući i napade na američke saveznike u Zalivu.
Regionalni zvaničnici su takođe u kontaktu s iranskim ministrom vanjskih poslova Abasom Aragčijem.
Najmanje jedna osoba poginula je u izraelskom vazdušnom napadu na stan u predgrađu Bejruta, Hazmije, saopštila je libanska nacionalna novinska agencija.
Izrael je više puta izvodio smrtonosne napade na gusto naseljena južna predgrađa Bejruta otkako je 2. marta počeo obnovljeni rat u Libanu, pri čemu je poginulo više od 1.000 ljudi, uključujući mnogo djece, više od 2.500 je ranjeno, a preko milion ljudi raseljeno.
Obnovljena izraelska ofanziva na Liban pokrenuta je nakon što je Hezbolah, libanska militantna grupa koju podržava Iran, ispalio rakete na sjever Izraela kao odgovor na ubistvo bivšeg iranskog vrhovnog vođe Alija Hamneija u zajedničkim američko-izraelskim vazdušnim napadima.

sources.news_title: Trump’s Ultimatum to Iran Escalates Tensions Over Strait of Hormuz – Pashto News and Current Affairs Channel
sources.text:
Trump’s ultimatum to Iran has sharply raised tensions in the Middle East, with both sides exchanging strong warnings over the Strait of Hormuz. The US has given Tehran 48 hours to reopen the vital shipping route or face possible strikes on its energy infrastructure.
US President Donald Trump warned that failure to act could lead to attacks on Iran’s power plants. In response, Iranian officials said any such move would trigger retaliation targeting US and allied infrastructure across the region.
Trump’s ultimatum to Iran comes at a time when the region is already on edge. Iranian missiles struck areas in southern Israel, causing injuries and damage near sensitive sites. The situation continues to worsen as both sides signal readiness to escalate further.
Iran has also warned that it could fully shut the Strait of Hormuz if its energy facilities come under attack. This route is critical for global oil shipments, and any disruption could send shockwaves through international markets.
Energy experts say the crisis has already started affecting supply chains. A significant share of global oil and gas flows through the strait, and ongoing tensions have raised fears of long-term instability in energy markets.
Global leaders are urging restraint. French President Emmanuel Macron called for an immediate halt to attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure. He stressed the need to restore safe navigation and avoid further escalation.
At the same time, political pressure is building in the United States. Senate leader Chuck Schumer called for an end to the conflict, saying concerns are growing even within US political circles.
Trump’s ultimatum to Iran has now become a turning point in the crisis. With both sides holding firm, the risk of a wider conflict remains high, while global markets and regional stability hang in the balance.

sources.news_title: REPORT: F-35 Pilot Suffered Shrapnel Wounds After Aircraft Was Hit Over Iran
sources.text:
REPORT: F-35 Pilot Suffered Shrapnel Wounds After Aircraft Was Hit Over Iran
YouTube / Ai TELLY
A US Air Force F-35A pilot sustained shrapnel wounds after their aircraft was struck during a combat mission over Iran on March 19, according to people familiar with the matter. The aircraft made an emergency landing at a base in the region. CENTCOM confirmed the landing and described the pilot as in stable condition but has declined to provide further details about the incident or the extent of damage to the aircraft.
What Hit the F-35
Given the altitude at which F-35s typically operate, officials familiar with the matter assess a surface-to-air missile as the most likely cause rather than small-arms fire. Iran’s IRGC posted a video on March 19 claiming to show an F-35 being targeted and struck by an Iranian air defense system. The video’s authenticity has not been confirmed.
Iran has developed air defense systems using passive infrared sensors rather than radar to track and engage aircraft. The approach bypasses the F-35’s stealth characteristics, which are designed to reduce radar cross-section rather than heat signature. Infrared-guided systems home in on engine heat regardless of an aircraft’s radar profile. The same sensor approach proved effective in Yemen where Iranian-backed Houthi forces used similar systems to shoot down approximately six MQ-9 Reapers during Operation Rough Rider last year.
Where This Fits in the Broader Loss Picture
The F-35 incident is one of approximately 20 US Air Force aircraft now known to have been damaged or destroyed in the nearly three-week conflict. Three F-15E Strike Eagles were shot down on March 2 in a friendly fire incident involving Kuwaiti F/A-18s. All crew members were recovered safely. On March 12 a KC-135 Stratotanker crashed in western Iraq killing all six crew members, with a second KC-135 sustaining severe tail damage in the same incident. At least one additional KC-135 was damaged on the ground by Iranian attacks in Saudi Arabia, a fact President Trump appeared to confirm in a March 14 social media post.
Approximately a dozen MQ-9 Reaper drones have been lost since the conflict began. Some were destroyed in the air. Others were damaged on the ground during Iranian missile and drone attacks on US bases in the region. The Reaper losses have not been formally announced by the Pentagon.
The pattern across all confirmed and reported losses shows that enemy fire has been most effective against uncrewed platforms, with manned aircraft losses coming primarily from accidents and friendly fire. The F-35 incident is the first confirmed case of a crewed aircraft being hit by Iranian fire with crew casualties resulting.

sources.news_title: Trump Wrote that He Had Productive Discussions with Iran About the War
sources.text:
Az elmúlt évtizedek legsúlyosabb energiaválságára figyelmeztetett Fatih Birol, a Nemzetközi Energiaügynökség (IEA) vezetője hétfőn, a sydney-i Nemzeti Sajtóklubban tartott beszédében az iráni háború következményei kapcsán.
Birol szerint a kialakult helyzet már most meghaladja az 1970-es évek két nagy olajválságának együttes hatását.
Elmondta, hogy míg a hetvenes évek olajválságai során egyenként mintegy napi 5 millió hordónyi kínálat esett ki, addig jelenleg napi 11 millió hordó olaj tűnt el a piacról. Ez a kiesés „több, mint a két nagy olajsokk együttvéve”. Az IEA-vezető „nagyon súlyosnak” nevezte a közel-keleti helyzetet, és hangsúlyozta: ha a válság tovább mélyül, egyetlen ország sem kerülheti el a hatásait.
A világgazdaság számára különösen nagy kockázatot jelent a Hormuzi-szoros blokádja, amelyen keresztül a globális tengeri olaj- és cseppfolyósítottgáz-szállítás mintegy ötöde halad át. A február 28-án kirobbant iráni háború kezdete óta a szorost gyakorlatilag lezárták. A blokád, valamint a térség olaj- és gázinfrastruktúráját érő iráni támadások jelentős áremelkedést váltottak ki a nemzetközi energiapiacokon.
A drágulás enyhítésére az IEA tagállamai március közepén rekordmennyiségű, mintegy 400-426 millió hordónyi kőolaj felszabadításáról döntöttek stratégiai készleteikből. Ez az intézkedés az ügynökség több mint 50 éves történetének eddigi legnagyobb tartalékfelhasználása, és a hatodik ilyen lépés.
Birol közölte: az IEA jelenleg további készletfelszabadítás lehetőségéről egyeztet ázsiai és európai kormányokkal. Hangsúlyozta, hogy nincs meghatározott olajárszint, amely automatikusan újabb beavatkozást váltana ki. A döntéseket a piaci helyzet folyamatos értékelése alapján hozzák meg. Az ügynökség vezetője szerint a válság kezelésének kulcsa a Hormuzi-szoros mielőbbi megnyitása lenne.
A legfontosabb megoldás ennek a problémának a rendezésére a szoros újranyitása
– fogalmazott.

sources.news_title: Trump: Postpones Attack on Iran for Five Days
sources.text:
I et innlegg på Truth Social mandag ettermiddag skriver USAs president Donald Trump at han har hatt «veldig gode og produktive samtaler med Iran».
Det står i kontrast til presidentens tidligere beskjed, der han ga iranske myndigheter en frist på 48 timer til å åpne Hormuzstredet eller få Irans energiinfrastruktur ødelagt.
De motstridende beskjedene har gitt svingninger på børsene mandag.
Det er usikkert om samtalene Trump skriver om, faktisk har skjedd. Mandag kveld avviser Irans parlamentariske leder Trumps uttalelser og klandrer den amerikanske presidenten for å dele falske nyheter.
Det er mye som skjer. I denne artikkelen kan du lese om disse siste utviklingene:
- Stup i oljeprisen
- Samtaler i kulissene
- Verdensøkonomi i fare
- Flere energianlegg skadet
- Trump truet med angrep
- Børsene som faller
Stup i oljeprisen
Trumps retrett har allerede fått konsekvenser for oljeprisen, som har sunket kraftig.
Mandag formiddag lå oljeprisen på rundt 113 dollar fatet. Etter Trumps retrett falt den derimot brått til et foreløpig bunnpunkt på 96 dollar fatet, før den hentet seg noe inn igjen.
Det har også fått konsekvenser for den norske kronen, som har svekket seg kraftig gjennom hele dagen.
– Nå er utsiktene for markedene bedret, sier sjeføkonom Harald Magnus Andreassen i Sparebank 1 Markets til NRK.
Han forklarer at endringene vi har sett i dag, kun skjer ved helt spesielle anledninger.
– Galskap er det selvfølgelig uansett. Og det gjør markedene fullstendig uforutsigbare.
Harald Magnus Andreassen
Sjeføkonom i Sparebank1 Markets.
Samtaler i kulissene
Midtøsten-ekspert Eirik Kvindesland omtaler Trumps kontrabeskjed mandag ettermiddag som en «stor hendelse».
– Det er muligens et gjennombrudd. Her har det tydeligvis vært samtaler i kulissene som vi ikke har kjent til, sier han til NRK.
Eirik Kvindesland
- Midtøsten-historiker og postdoktor på Institutt for Iran-studier ved Det østerrikske vitenskapsakademi
- Forfatter av boken Iran og Israel: Gamle venner, nye fiender (2025)
Trumps trussel om å angripe Iran innen 48 timer skapte global uro.
Da Axios skrev at USA også vurderte å okkupere den iranske øya Kharg, truet det iranske forsvarsrådet med å minelegge Persiabukta.
Truslene fra begge parter har vært troverdige, mener Kvindesland. Han tror det kan være en årsak til at Trump nå drar i bremsen:
– Han har sannsynligvis blitt pressa ganske hardt av allierte. Antakeligvis de arabiske golfstatene, og sikkert andre. Nå er dette så alvorlig og katastrofalt at det risikerer jo ikke bare Trumps eget presidentskap, men òg hele verdensøkonomien, sier han.
Midtøsten-eksperten mener det fortsatt er mange skjær i sjøen for en eventuell diplomatisk løsning.
– Så langt vet vi ikke om disse samtalene faktisk har pågått, eller om dette er Trump som egenhending kaster inn håndkleet.
Verdensøkonomien i fare
Hele verdens økonomi står i stor fare på grunn av energikrisen i Midtøsten, advarer sjefen for Det internasjonale energibyrået (IEA), Fatih Birol.
Krigen i regionen skaper store problemer for energiforsyningen, spesielt rundt Hormuzstredet.
Birol sier at ingen land vil slippe unna konsekvensene hvis krisen fortsetter.
– Verdensøkonomien står overfor en svært stor trussel i dag, sa Birol under et møte i Australia mandag, ifølge nyhetsbyrået AFP.
Han mener det nå trengs en felles innsats fra hele verden for å løse situasjonen raskest mulig.
Norges statsminister Jonas Gahr Støre (Ap) er enig med IEA-sjefen.
– Ytterligere opptrapping kan få alvorlige konsekvenser for verdensøkonomien, sa Støre til NRK tidligere mandag.
– De ansvarlige lederne må nå tenke grundig gjennom det ansvaret de har.
Flere energianlegg skadet
Birol opplyser også om at minst 40 viktige energianlegg er «alvorlig skadet» som følge av krigen i Midtøsten.
Skadene påvirker produksjon og frakt av energi i regionen. Meldingen kommer samtidig som Israel har bekreftet omfattende luftangrep mot iransk infrastruktur.
– Det er ingen tvil om at det vil være et sjokk for verdensøkonomien hvis store mengder av all tilgjengelig råolje i verden blir borte, pluss flytende naturgass, gjødsel, aluminium og andre produkter fra Gulfen, sa økonom Andreassen tidligere mandag.
Ifølge ham vil konsekvensen være at industrier som bruker olje, må redusere aktiviteten.
– En sånn situasjon har vi ikke hatt tidligere. Det er dramatisk.
Hormuzstredet
Hva er Hormuzstredet og hvor ligger det? Hormuzstredet er en av verdens viktigste skipsruter for transport av olje.
Stredet går mellom Iran og Oman, og deler Persiabukta fra resten av Arabiahavet.
Gjennom stredet, som på sitt smaleste er i underkant av fem mil bredt, fraktes en femtedel av verdens olje og gass.
I 2025 ble rundt 20 millioner fat olje fraktet gjennom Hormuzstredet hver dag, ifølge det amerikanske energidepartementet. Det tilsvarer energihandel for nær 600 milliarder dollar i året.
Oljen kommer ikke bare fra Iran, men også fra Irak, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi-Arabia og De forente arabiske emirater.
Hvorfor er Hormuzstredet viktig i krigen mellom USA, Israel og Iran? – Hormuzstredet er et av de stedene som det er enklest for Iran å påvirke militært og som har stor effekt på verdensøkonomien, som igjen kan påvirke USA ved å skape uro i verdensmarkedene, forteller Kyrre Tromm Lindvig.
Han er hovedlærer ved seksjon for strategi og fellesoperasjoner ved Forsvarets Høgskole.
Kort tid etter at USA og Israel gikk til angrep på Iran, truet Iran med å «stenge» Hormuzstredet og sette fyr på alle skip som forsøkte å passere.
USAs president Donald Trump har advart om at Washington vil slå enda hardere tilbake dersom Iran blokkerer oljeeksporten.
Hvorfor skjer det angrep ved Hormuzstredet nå? Lindvig forklarer at Iran har mistet mye av sin evne til å angripe med avanserte missiler, som tidligere ble brukt mot mål i Gulf‑statene, USA og Israel.
– Med Hormuzstredet kan Iran fremdeles påvirke militært på en veldig effektiv måte med relativt enkle midler, slik som droner, småbåter og miner, sier Lindvig.
Iran mener at alle amerikanske eller israelske skip, eller skip som frakter olje for de to landene, er legitime mål.
Hittil er det meldt om minst 14 angrep mot skip i Hormuzstredet de siste to ukene.
Onsdag ble lasteskip som seilte under flaggene til Thailand, Japan og Marshalløyene angrepet.
Den iranske revolusjonsgarden innrømmer å ha stått bak angrepet på det Thailandske skipet.
Hva er konsekvensen av å stenge Hormuzstredet? Siden krigen startet har så godt som all skipstrafikk gjennom Hormuzstredet stått på pause.
Det fører til at transporten av olje og gass, stoppes opp.
Når trafikken forstyrres, hopper olje- og gassprisene kraftig, noe som igjen har stor effekt på verdens aksjemarkeder, forklarer Lundvig.
Analysebyrået Wood Mackenzie venter oljepriser på 150 dollar fatet de neste ukene, forutsatt at Hormuzstredet forblir stengt. De advarer også om at prisen kan stige til 200 dollar fatet i løpet av 2026. Før krigen lå prisene på omkring 70 dollar per fat.
I tillegg må flere produsenter redusere produksjonen fordi lagrene deres fylles opp når eksporten stopper opp, forklarer Lindvig.
Irak, Qatar og Kuwait er noen av landene som har bestemt seg for å redusere produksjonen av olje og gass.
Hvis situasjonen i Hormuzstredet vedvarer vil det vil være 20 prosent mindre olje og gass i verden enn vi er vant til.
Asia og Europa er de de mest sårbare regionene for forsyningsforstyrrelser, og er mer avhengig av import av råolje, gass og drivstoff fra Midtøsten enn andre deler av verden.
Trump truet med angrep
Natt til søndag la Trump ut den meldingen på Truth Social med advarsel om at USA kom til å angripe Irans største kraftverk innen to døgn, om landet ikke åpnet Hormuzstredet.
– Hvis Iran ikke åpner opp Hormuzstredet fullstendig, uten noen trusler, innen 48 timer fra nøyaktig dette tidspunktet, kommer USA til å angripe og utslette de ulike kraftverkene deres, og det største blir det første. Takk for oppmerksomheten, skrev presidenten da.
Tidsfristen skulle gått ut 01:44 natt til tirsdag 24. mars, men dette angrepet skal nå være satt på pause i fem dager, ifølge presidenten selv.
Iranske militærmyndigheter kom også med en egen trussel mot Trump.
Hvis Irans drivstoff- og energiinfrastruktur blir angrepet, kommer all energiinfrastruktur tilhørende USA i regionen til å være mål for iranske angrep, het det i en uttalelse viderebrakt av iranske medier. Iran truet med å ramme både energi- og avsaltingsanlegg i regionen.
Senere sa de at Iran vil samarbeide med IMO for delvis å gjenåpne Hormuzstredet og beskytte sjøfolk i Persiabukta.
Kraftig børsfall
Trumps trussel om flere angrep fikk konsekvenser for verdensbørsene mandag morgen. Det var blant annet kraftig fall ved flere av Asia-børsene.
Handelsdagen endte med et fall på nesten 3,5 prosent på Nikkei-indeksen i Tokyo, mens den bredere Topix-indeksen endte ned 3,4 prosent.
I Seoul i Sør-Korea falt Kospi-indeksen med hele 6,5 prosent, ifølge NTB, mens Hang Seng-indeksen i Hongkong stengte ned 3,5 prosent og hovedindeksen i Shanghai falt 3,6 prosent.
Også Oslo Børs har en tøff handelsdag og åpnet ned 1,3 prosent like etter åpningstid. Selv om Europa-børsene har hentet seg noe inn i løpet av ettermiddagen, er det fortsatt røde tall i Oslo.
– Norge tjener på krigen, derfor går Oslo Børs opp når oljeprisen er høy. Krigen er ikke bra for norsk økonomi og næringsliv, men Norge har flere bedrifter som tjener på prisstigning på olje enn andre land, sier økonom Andreassen.

sources.news_title: Iran threatens Strait of Hormuz closure amid US strike warning - SABC News - Breaking news, special reports, world, business, sport coverage of all South African current events. Africa's news leader.
sources.text:
Iran warned it would strike energy and water infrastructure across the Gulf if US President Donald Trump follows through on his threat to attack its electricity grid, raising fears of mass disruption in a region heavily dependent on desalination for drinking water.
Trump set a Monday deadline of around 7:45 p.m. EDT (2345 GMT), warning late on Saturday that the United States would strike Iran’s power plants unless Tehran fully reopened the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours.
US President Donald Trump and Iran threatened to escalate their war, targeting energy and fuel facilities in the Gulf, which could again roil global energy and financial markets and deepen a regional crisis. https://t.co/7yJWCxhGkQ pic.twitter.com/ywQrXMDUaY
— SABC News (@SABCNews) March 22, 2026
The prospect of tit-for-tat strikes on civilian infrastructure further unsettled oil markets, with prices opening choppy, in Asia trading.
After more than three weeks of heavy US and Israeli bombardment that officials say has sharply reduced Iran’s missile capabilities, Tehran has continued to demonstrate its ability to strike back.
Air raid sirens sounded across parts of northern and central Israel, including in Tel Aviv, and the occupied West Bank overnight, on Sunday warning of incoming missiles from Iran. The Israeli military said early Monday it had begun a wide-scale wave of strikes targeting Iranian infrastructure in Tehran.
Iranian news agencies said at least one child was killed and several people were injured in the bombing of a residential area in western Khorramabad city.
A residential neighbourhood, in the northwestern city of Urmia was damaged by an air strike, Iranian news agencies reported. Iranian Red Crescent rescuers were shown in a video searching for survivors. There were no immediate reports of casualties.
Trump’s warning came less than a day after he signaled the US might be considering winding down the conflict, even as US Marines and heavy landing craft were heading to the region.
“If Iran’s fuel and energy infrastructure is attacked by the enemy, all energy infrastructure, as well as information technology…and water desalination facilities, belonging to the US and the regime in the region will be targeted pursuant to previous warnings,” Iranian military spokesperson, Ebrahim Zolfaqari said, according to state media.
While attacks on electricity could hurt Iran, they could be catastrophic for its Gulf neighbours, which consume around five times as much power per capita.
Electricity makes their gleaming desert cities habitable, in part by powering the desalination plants that produce 100% of the water consumed in Bahrain and Qatar. Such plants use seawater to meet more than 80% of drinking water needs in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and 50% of the water supply in Saudi Arabia.
Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf doubled down, writing on X that critical infrastructure and energy facilities in the Middle East could be “irreversibly destroyed” should Iranian power plants be attacked.
Iran’s powerful Revolutionary Guards said it would also mean the shipping lane where a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas normally transits along Iran’s southern coast would remain shut.
“The Strait of Hormuz will be completely closed and will not be opened until our destroyed power plants are rebuilt,” the Guards said in a statement.
The Saudi defence ministry said, early Monday two ballistic missiles had been launched towards Riyadh. One missile was intercepted while the other fell in an uninhabited area.
On Sunday, Iranian strikes on two southern Israeli towns injured dozens in what an Israeli hospital described as a major casualty event. The towns were located close to Israel’s secretive nuclear reactor and a number of military installations, including Nevatim Air Base, one of the country’s largest.
More than 2,000 people have been killed during the war the US and Israel launched on February 28, which has upended markets, spiked fuel costs, fuelled global inflation fears and convulsed the postwar Western alliance.
‘TICKING TIME BOMB OF ELEVATED UNCERTAINTY’
“President Trump’s threat has now placed a 48-hour ticking time bomb of elevated uncertainty over markets,” said IG market analyst Tony Sycamore, who expects stock markets to fall when they reopen on Monday.
Iranian attacks have effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, causing the worst oil crisis since the 1970s. Its near-closure sent European gas prices surging as much as 35% last week.
“If Iran doesn’t FULLY OPEN, WITHOUT THREAT, the Strait of Hormuz, within 48 HOURS from this exact point in time, the United States of America will hit and obliterate their various POWER PLANTS, STARTING WITH THE BIGGEST ONE FIRST!” Trump posted on social media around 7:45 p.m. EDT (2345 GMT), on Saturday.
Iranian media quoted the country’s representative to the International Maritime Organisation as saying the strait remains open to all shipping except vessels linked to “Iran’s enemies”.
Ali Mousavi said passage through the waterway was possible by coordinating security and safety arrangements with Tehran.
Ship-tracking data shows some vessels, such as Indian-flagged ships and a Pakistani oil tanker, have negotiated safe passage through the strait.
‘WEEKS MORE FIGHTING’
The war has been taking place alongside a confrontation on a separate front between Israel and Lebanon’s Hezbollah, backed by Iran.
Israel said on Sunday its troops had raided a number of the armed group’s sites in southern Lebanon.
Israeli military spokesperson Brigadier General Effie Defrin told reporters Israel expects “weeks more of fighting against Iran and Hezbollah.”
Hezbollah said it had attacked several border areas in northern Israel. Israeli emergency services said one person was killed in a kibbutz near the border. Israel later said it was checking whether the death was caused by Israeli fire.
Hezbollah has fired hundreds of rockets at Israel since it entered the regional war on March 2, prompting an Israeli offensive that has killed more than 1000 people in Lebanon.

sources.news_title: Global Energy Crisis Deepens as Battle for Hormuz Escalates Under Trump Ultimatum
sources.text:
THE PERSIAN GULF — The world stands at the precipice of an unprecedented energy catastrophe as the “Battle for Hormuz” enters a decisive and perilous new phase. Following three weeks of de facto blockade and maritime skirmishes, the conflict has shifted from a localized naval confrontation into a global economic emergency. On Saturday, March 21, 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump issued a final 48-hour ultimatum from his Mar-a-Lago club to the Iranian regime: fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping or face the “obliteration” of Iran’s domestic power grid.
U.S. forces continue to eliminate the Iranian regime’s one-way attack drone capabilities, which they’ve used to indiscriminately target civilians throughout the region. pic.twitter.com/AbdLMmtoei
— U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) March 22, 2026
America is firmly in control of the Iran conflict, and we have demolished Iran’s capability for aggression.@POTUS, @SecWar, and General Caine are spearheading our campaign to destroy all fortifications along the Strait of Hormuz. pic.twitter.com/jH6cLqh1vo
— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) March 22, 2026
The stakes have never been higher for the American consumer. As of Sunday, March 22, the national average for a gallon of regular gasoline has surged to $3.94. However, the crisis is hitting closer to the President’s home more than most – in Palm Beach County, Florida, where Mar-a-Lago is located, prices at the pump have already breached the psychological barrier, with averages sitting at $4.08 per gallon. Some premium stations in West Palm Beach are reporting prices as high as $4.45, reflecting the market’s panic as 20% of the world’s oil supply remains trapped behind the Iranian-controlled chokepoint.
Iran’s Counter-Threat: A Regional Blackout
Tehran has not flinched. Following the U.S. ultimatum, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and high-ranking Iranian officials issued a chilling response. Iran’s Parliament Speaker, Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, warned that if the United States strikes Iranian power plants, “all energy, information technology, and desalination infrastructure” belonging to the U.S. and its allies in the region will be considered legitimate targets for “irreversible destruction.”
Military commanders in Tehran further clarified that if their energy grid is compromised, they will move to “completely close” the Strait of Hormuz—not just through the current threat of harassment, but through a total physical and military blockade. This “energy war” strategy threatens to plunge the entire Middle East into darkness, affecting water desalination plants that provide drinking water for millions.
The Houthi Wildcard: The Red Sea Front
Adding a second layer of pressure to the crisis, the Houthi movement in Yemen has signaled its intent to re-enter the fray. Having largely observed a period of relative calm following the 2025 Gaza peace plan, Houthi leadership announced on February 28, 2026, that they would escalate in solidarity with Iran.
Intelligence reports indicate that the Houthis have moved advanced missile and drone launchers into the mountainous regions of Al-Hudaydah and Hajjah, overlooking the Red Sea. Their objective is clear: to shut down the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, effectively creating a dual-chokepoint crisis that would sever the primary maritime artery between Europe and Asia. If both the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea are closed, the global shipping industry faces a total collapse of the Suez Canal route, forcing vessels into the long and costly journey around the Cape of Good Hope.
A Chokepoint Under Siege
The physical “Battle for Hormuz” has already seen significant losses. Since the outbreak of hostilities on February 28:
- Shipping Collapse: Daily transits through the Strait have plummeted by 94%.
- Casualties at Sea: At least 12 merchant ships have been damaged, and 12 seafarers are reported killed or missing.

Tensions in the Middle East have intensified after Iran released a video claiming its air defense system targeted and brought down a US F-15 fighter jet near the Strait of Hormuz.
According to Iranian state media, the incident took place close to the country’s southern coastline and near Hormuz Island. Officials from Iran’s Joint Air Defense Command stated that the aircraft had launched a missile before being struck by Iranian defenses. Authorities added that further details about the aircraft are still being gathered.
Despite the reported attack, Iranian sources claimed that surveillance activity continues, with Israeli and American drones still operating in the region.
In a separate statement, Iranian television also reported that airstrikes on central parts of the country have reduced following what it described as an earlier attack on a US F-35 fighter jet.
The situation comes amid ongoing conflict that began on February 28, when joint operations by the United States and Israel targeted sites inside Iran. According to Iranian reports, more than 1,300 people have been killed in these attacks, including senior leadership figures.
In response, Iran has launched a series of drone and missile strikes aimed at US-linked military positions in Israel, as well as in neighboring countries such as Jordan, Iraq, and several Gulf states. The developments signal a dangerous escalation, raising concerns about wider instability in the region.

sources.news_title: Iran warns Strait of Hormuz will be "completely closed" if US targets power plants
sources.text:
Iran warns Strait of Hormuz will be “completely closed” if US targets power plants
TEHRAN: Iran on Sunday warned that the strategic Strait of Hormuz would be “completely closed” and the energy infrastructure of Israel and the Gulf countries in the region that host American bases would be “legitimate targets” if the US hits the country’s power plants.
In a statement quoted by Iran’s state media, Press TV, Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari, said the Strait of Hormuz is “closed only to the enemy” but will be “completely” closed if the “terrorist” American President acts on his threats.
The Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters is Iran’s highest operational command unit that coordinates operations between the Army and the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC).
“The terrorist American President, continuing his aggressive behaviour and efforts to destabilise the world, has threatened that if Iran does not open the Strait of Hormuz, he will target Iran’s power plants. We have said repeatedly that the Strait of Hormuz is closed only to the enemy and to harmful traffic, and it has not yet been fully closed. It remains under our intelligent control, and harmless passage occurs under specific regulations that ensure our security and interests,” Zolfaghari said.
“The Strait of Hormuz will be completely closed, and it will not be reopened until our destroyed power plants are rebuilt,” the spokesperson said as quoted by Press TV.
He further warned that “All power plants, energy infrastructure, and information technology (ICT) infrastructure of the Zionist regime will be extensively targeted,” and added that “the power plants of countries in the region that host American bases will be legitimate targets for us.”
Zolfaghari also warned that “All similar companies in the region that have American shareholders will be completely destroyed,” as quoted by Press TV.
He added, ” Everything is ready for the great struggle aimed at the complete destruction of all American economic interests in the West Asia region.”
Emphasising that Iran does not seek conflict, the spokesperson said, “We were not the initiators of war, nor will we be now. However, if the enemy damages our power plants, we will do whatever it takes to defend our country and the interests of our nation. “
“The relentless process of destroying the specified targets will begin, and nothing will be able to stop the continuation of our operations to destroy the energy, oil, and industrial infrastructure of America and its allies in the region,” Zolfaghari added, according to Press TV.
Earlier, US President Donald Trump warned Iran of obliterating its power plants if it fails to open the Strait of Hormuz. Trump gave Iran precisely 48 hours for the job.
“If Iran doesn’t FULLY OPEN, WITHOUT THREAT, the Strait of Hormuz, within 48 HOURS from this exact point in time, the United States of America will hit and obliterate their various POWER PLANTS, STARTING WITH THE BIGGEST ONE FIRST! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP,” he said in a post on Truth Social.

【大紀元2026年03月23日訊】（英文大紀元記者Jacob Burg報導／陳霆編譯）伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊週日（3月22日）表示，若美國總統川普攻擊伊朗的能源設施，伊朗將動手封鎖整個霍爾木茲海峽。
川普週六在社群媒體發文指出，若德黑蘭當局未能在發文後的48小時內，在「不受威脅的情況下」全面開放霍爾木茲海峽，美軍將會「打擊並摧毀（伊朗）各座發電廠，並從最大的一座開始下手」。
在此消息發布的前一天，川普曾表示美國在中東對伊朗的軍事目標「即將達成」，並稱在戰爭進入第四週後，他將考慮「逐步結束」這場衝突。
革命衛隊在週日的聲明中強調：「霍爾木茲海峽將被完全封鎖，在我們被摧毀的發電廠重建完成之前，絕不會重新開放。」
革命衛隊警告，若華府攻擊伊朗能源設施，任何美資持股的公司都將遭到「徹底摧毀」。聲明同時聲稱，駐有美軍的國家，其能源基礎設施也將成為「合法」打擊目標。
伊朗週日進一步威脅，若川普履行其48小時最後通牒，伊朗將打擊波斯灣鄰國的能源與供水設施。
川普在週六的聲明中強調，霍爾木茲海峽「應由其它使用該水道的國家視需求自行守衛與巡邏——美國不會代勞！」
他表示：「若有國家提出請求，我們會協助其在霍爾木茲海峽的行動，但一旦伊朗的威脅被消除，這將不再有其必要。重要的是，對這些國家而言，這將是一場輕而易舉的軍事行動。」
儘管美國進口的石油中僅有極小部分經由霍爾木茲海峽運輸，但全球約有20%的石油及液化天然氣，都必須通過這條關鍵水道。
伊朗總統佩澤什基安（Masoud Pezeshkian）週日在社群媒體發布聲明稱，「除了侵犯（伊朗）領土的人之外」，霍爾木茲海峽對所有人都是開放的。
目前，伊朗已實際對所有未明確向其政權尋求安全通行的船隻關閉海峽。全球石油供應的中斷，已引發市場劇烈波動與不確定性。
截至週日上午，由於海峽仍處於封鎖狀態，國際基準油價布倫特原油已攀升至每桶112.19美元。伊朗領導人聲稱，若戰爭持續，油價恐怕會飆升至每桶200美元。
包括中國、印度與日本在內的許多亞洲經濟體，都高度依賴經由該海峽運輸的能源。
日本外務大臣茂木敏充週日表示，若美國、以色列能與伊朗達成停火，日本或許會考慮派遣自衛隊在霍爾木茲海峽執行掃雷任務。
茂木在富士電視台的節目中提到：「若能達成全面停火，那麼掃雷這類行動就可能被列入討論。」
他補充道：「這純屬假設。但如果停火協議順利達成，而水雷又構成航行障礙，我認為這將是值得考慮的選項。」
茂木表示，日本目前暫無計劃針對受困日本船隻的通行安排進行協商。他強調，確保所有船隻都能安全通過這條狹窄水道是「極其重要」的。
不過，伊朗外長阿拉格齊（Abbas Araqchi）上週五曾告訴日本共同社，他已與茂木敏充商討，可能允許日本船隻安全通過該海峽。
日本約有90%的石油運輸依賴這條海峽。由於德黑蘭當局目前已實質關閉這條水道，不斷攀升的全球油價已迫使日本及其它國家開始釋出石油儲備。
週六，阿聯酋也加入各國行列，承諾支持在霍爾木茲海峽建立安全通道。
阿聯酋與其它二十多個國家在週六發布聯合聲明指出：「我們表示，願為確保海峽安全通行做出應有努力。」
阿聯酋表示：「我們歡迎各國積極參與相關的籌備與規劃工作。」
原文： Iran Threatens to Close Entire Hormuz Strait, Strike Utilities, US Companies After Trump Ultimatum 刊登於英文《大紀元時報》。

sources.news_title: Iran Threatens Gulf Energy, Water in Escalating Tensions
sources.text:
Iran’s threat to cripple Gulf energy and water infrastructure in retaliation for any U.S. strike on its power grid exposes a fragile regional interdependence where civilian resilience is tenuously balanced against geopolitical brinkmanship. The warning from Iranian military spokesman Ebrahim Zolfaqari—broadcast late Saturday—signals a deliberate escalation that could turn civilian infrastructure into collateral damage, with desalination plants and electricity grids emerging as the next battleground.
The stakes are existential for the Gulf states. Desalination, which supplies nearly all of Bahrain and Qatar’s drinking water and over 80% in the UAE and half in Saudi Arabia, depends entirely on uninterrupted power. A coordinated attack on Iran’s energy grid, even if justified as a military response, would inevitably trigger reciprocal strikes on regional facilities. Iran has already demonstrated its asymmetric reach, with Revolutionary Guards vowing to close the Strait of Hormuz—through which one-fifth of global oil and LNG passes—until its power plants are restored. The closure is not merely a threat; it is a plausible scenario that would send shockwaves through energy markets still reeling from three weeks of sustained bombardment.
The timing of Trump’s ultimatum—delivered via social media at 7:45 p.m. EDT on Saturday—was itself a calculated move, compressing the decision window to 48 hours and injecting maximum uncertainty into already volatile markets. Oil prices, which had surged as much as 35% last week amid fears of Strait closure, opened choppy in early Asian trading. IG market analyst Tony Sycamore described the president’s declaration as a “ticking time bomb of elevated uncertainty,” a phrase that understates the potential for cascading economic damage. Traders are pricing in not just supply disruptions but the broader risk of a regional blackout that could paralyze trade, finance, and logistics across the Arabian Peninsula.
Israel’s role in this escalation complicates the calculus. While the U.S. and Israel claim to have degraded Iran’s missile and drone capabilities through sustained air strikes, Iran’s retaliatory actions—including a rare 4,000-km ballistic missile strike on a U.S.-British base in the Indian Ocean—demonstrate that Tehran retains the ability to project force beyond its borders. The overnight missile alerts across northern and central Israel, including Tel Aviv, underscore how quickly civilian centers can become targets. The targeting of southern Israeli towns near Nevatim Air Base, a key strategic installation, suggests Iran is not merely retaliating against military assets but probing vulnerabilities in Israel’s civil infrastructure.
The interlinking of energy, water, and military strategy creates a feedback loop where any strike on power plants could spiral into a humanitarian crisis. Gulf Cooperation Council economies, already grappling with inflation and fiscal strain, would face immediate pressure on sovereign credit ratings as investors reassess the stability of essential services. Water rationing and blackouts could trigger social unrest, particularly in densely populated urban centers like Riyadh and Dubai, where desalination plants operate at near-full capacity.
What remains unclear is whether Iran’s threats are primarily deterrent or operational. The Revolutionary Guards’ vow to keep the Strait closed “until our destroyed power plants are rebuilt” implies a conditional stance—one that could be dialed down if concessions are offered. Yet the same statement frames the closure as a fait accompli, raising the risk of miscalculation. The fact that some vessels, including Indian and Pakistani ships, have negotiated passage suggests a degree of selective engagement, but the absence of major oil tankers from the strait points to a de facto blockade.
For markets, the overriding question is duration. A short-lived closure of the Strait, even if damaging, could be absorbed by strategic petroleum reserves and rerouted shipping. But a prolonged disruption—lasting weeks or months—would force a structural shift in global oil flows, pushing Brent crude toward $100 per barrel and deepening stagflationary pressures in Europe and Asia. European gas prices, which surged last week, would likely retest highs, while U.S. gasoline futures could spike ahead of the summer driving season.
The human cost is already visible. Over 2,000 lives lost since February 28, the displacement of communities near frontlines in Lebanon and Gaza, and the psychological toll of constant air raid sirens in Israeli cities paint a picture of a conflict that has moved beyond proportional response. Iran’s strategy appears to be one of calibrated escalation—using civilian infrastructure as both a shield and a sword—while the U.S. and Israel rely on technological superiority to limit Iran’s counterstrikes.

sources.news_title: Iran. Iranian Government Warns that It Will Completely Shut Down Ormuz if the Us Attacks Its Energy Infrastructure - Latin American Summary
sources.text:
Irán. Gobierno iraní advierte que cerrará totalmente Ormuz si EE.UU. ataca su infraestructura energética
TeleSUR, Resumen Latinoamericano, 22 de marzo de 2026.
Mientras ejecutaba la oleada 74 de la Operación Promesa Veraz contra bases estadounidenses en Medio Oriente y áreas israelíes en el centro y sur de los territorios ocupados, Irán advirtió este domingo que cerrará completamente el estratégica estrecho de Ormuz si su infraestructura energética es atacada.
El sábado, Donald Trump dio a Teherán un plazo de 48 horas para “abrir” el estrecho bajo amenaza de atacar las centrales eléctricas iraníes, “¡empezando con la más grande!”. Irán respondió prometiendo que, en ese caso, atacaría instalaciones energéticas y desalinizadoras que sirven a EE.UU. en la región.
Este domingo, la nación persa ha sumado un escalón más con la advertencia de cierre total de Ormuz.
El presidente de #EstadosUnidos, Donald Trump, hizo un llamado a potencias del mundo para que ayuden a restablecer el paso por el estrecho de #Ormuz. #Irán ha cerrado este importante paso marítimo producto de la agresión de #EEUU e #Israel contra la nación persa. pic.twitter.com/JTg6jM3Pln
— teleSUR TV (@teleSURtv) March 17, 2026
De acuerdo con expertos legales, las reglas del derecho internacional indican que solo se puede atacar centrales eléctricas al servicio de poblaciones civiles si la ventaja militar supera el sufrimiento que se causa a la población.
Al anunciar la intención de Teherán de cerrar por completo Ormuz si se ataca su infraestructura energética, el teniente coronel Ebrahim Zolfaqari, portavoz del Cuartel General Central de Khatam al-Anbiya, reiteró que la vía marítima está cerrada “únicamente al paso enemigo y perjudicial” y que está “bajo nuestro control inteligente”, permitiendo “el paso seguro” a “embarcaciones que no estén relacionadas con los enemigos”.
“El tránsito no perjudicial continúa bajo regulaciones específicas que garantizan nuestra seguridad e intereses”, agregó el portavoz.
De acuerdo con fuentes especializadas de la industria, por Ormuz —que conecta el golfo Pérsico con el resto del mundo y es vía de tránsito de un quinto del petróleo que se comercializa a nivel mundial, una quinta parte de los envíos de GNL y un tercio del fertilizante más usado— transitaban diariamente 138 barcos antes de la guerra. Desde el 28 de febrero, inicio de los ataques israelo-estadounidenses y las represalias iraníes, el tráfico se ha reducido en más de un 95%.
En las poco más de tres semanas transcurridas desde entonces, menos de un centenar de buques han transitado Ormuz (un promedio de cinco o seis por día), la mayoría de bandera iraní o bajo instrucciones y guía de las autoridades de Teherán.
En sus declaraciones de este domingo, el portavoz del Cuartel General Central de Khatam al-Anbiya —organismo responsable de la planificación, coordinación operativa y despliegue de las fuerzas armadas—, recalcó que si se atacan sus instalaciones energéticas, Irán “cerrará completamente el estrecho de Ormuz hasta que se reconstruyan las instalaciones dañadas”.
Agregó que todos los centros de generación de electricidad, la infraestructura energética y los sistemas de tecnología de la información y la comunicación (TIC) de Israel serían el objetivo. Igualmente, serían objetivos legítimos las empresas similares con accionistas estadounidenses en la región y las centrales eléctricas en los países de la región que albergan bases estadounidenses.
SIPRI Senior Researcher @PWezeman explains how US arms exports strengthen global influence, serving as both a foreign policy tool and a driver of the US defence industry. Watch now🎥#SIPRI #ArmsTransfers #ArmsTrade pic.twitter.com/HZgKO0k3Yx
— SIPRI (@SIPRIorg) March 16, 2026
También este domingo, el Servicio de Inteligencia del Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica (CGRI) respondió a la amenaza de Trump y afirmó que los centros tecnológicos críticos fuera de la región serán atacados en un plazo de 48 horas si se golpea la planta energética iraní.
A partir de ahora, declaró el Servicio, “las fuerzas armadas de Irán también tienen en la mira objetivos tecnológicos y políticos extrarregionales asociados con los enemigos de la República Islámica”.
En X, el presidente Masoud Pezeshkian publicó que “las amenazas y el terror no hacen más que reforzar nuestra unidad (…) La ilusión de borrar a Irán del mapa muestra desesperación frente a la voluntad de una nación que hace historia”. Recalcó, además, que por ahora Ormuz “está abierto a todos, excepto a quienes violan nuestro territorio”.
Guerra contra Irán golpea energía, economía y prospectos de crecimiento globales
The New York Times informó el viernes que al menos 39 refinerías de petróleo, yacimientos de gas natural y otras instalaciones energéticas en nueve países han sido dañados desde el comienzo de la guerra.
La perturbación del tráfico en Ormuz a raíz de la guerra ha afectado el suministro energético global y ya tiene impactos en la economía mundial, con un aumento drástico de los precios de la energía y su reflejo transversal en otros sectores, incluso en Estados Unidos, donde los consumidores están siendo gravemente afectados.
Esta semana, la OMC ha señalado que si la guerra se prolonga durante el resto de 2026, se prevé un crecimiento del 2.5% este año, inferior al 2.8% anterior previsto.
La Organización Mundial del Comercio advirtió que los flujos comerciales mundiales y el crecimiento económico se ralentizarán más de lo previsto si el aumento de los precios de la energía y las interrupciones en el transporte causadas por el conflicto en Oriente Medio se prolongan.
Continúan ataques contra Irán y represalias iraníes
Este domingo, el Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica (CGRI) de Irán ha informado sobre el lanzamiento de la 74 oleada de la Operación Promesa Veraz 4 contra bases militares estadounidenses en la región y emplazamientos israelíes en zonas del sur de los territorios palestinos ocupados.
El CGRI notificó el lanzamiento de misiles balísticos Emad, Fateh y Qiam, así como drones de ataque, contra la base aérea Príncipe Sultán en Arabia Saudita, la Quinta Flota en Bahréin y una posición utilizada por los militantes kurdos de Komala, en el norte de Irak. Además, bases militares y centros de seguridad en Tel Aviv, Petah Tikva, Holon y Ramat Gan, en Israel, fueron atacados, en una operación en que fueron usados misiles pesados, incluidos los sistemas Ghadr, Kheibar Shekan y Khorramshahr-4.
Durante la jornada, el ejército israelí lanzó ataques a gran escala sobre Teherán. Los ataques cruzados de las últimas horas han elevado el número de víctimas mortales en Irán, Israel y Líbano, bajo ataque sionista.
Al menos 210 niños han muerto y otros 1.510 han resultado heridos en Irán desde el inicio de la guerra, según fuentes sanitarias del país. Fuentes externas cifran en más de 1.400 los civiles muertos.
En Líbano, los ataques de Israel han provocado más de un millar de muertos y una cifra superior al medio millón de desplazados.
Los ataques contra Israel causaron 15 muertos en territorio israelí y cuatro en Cisjordania ocupada.
El Pentágono admite el incremento de bajas en sus filas tras 10 días de contraofensiva iraní, mientras Teherán denuncia la censura informativa de Washington sobre el impacto real de la guerra.https://t.co/k7dHbE6R3x

Irán y Trump: una “breve excursión” que se complica y levanta riesgos en casa
Los desafíos y represalias efectivas de Irán han continúan luego de tres semanas de ataques cruzados con Israel y Estados Unidos, mientras analistas siguen señalando los errores de cálculo y la falta de una estrategia de salida clara para el jefe de la Casa Blanca, que enfrenta incertidumbre en el frente, críticas en el ámbito nacional y un control mermado sobre sus seguidores MAGA.
El despliegue de más tropas en Medio Oriente para posibles operaciones terrestres —con el riesgo de más bajas—, el alza de los precios de la gasolina, la energía y productos de consumo, amenazan aún más el debilitado índice de aprobación de Trump y las perspectivas de los republicanos en la carrera a las elecciones de medio término, a lo que se suma la brecha abierta entre Washington y sus aliados de la OTAN, a los que calificó de “cobardes” por negarse a intervenir en el estrecho de Ormuz.
“Trump se ha metido en un lío con la guerra contra Irán y no sabe cómo salir de él”, dijo Aaron David Miller, exnegociador para Oriente Medio en Administraciones republicanas y demócratas. “Esa es su mayor fuente de frustración”, comentó.
La guerra en Oriente Medio y la creciente inseguridad están alterando las rutas mundiales de transporte marítimo y de suministro, lo que está encareciendo los alimentos, el combustible y el transporte.

sources.news_title: Iran threatens to 'completely' close Hormuz and hit power plants after Trump ultimatum
sources.text:
Arad (Israel)
The United States and Iran have threatened to target critical infrastructure as the war in the Middle East, now in its fourth week, puts lives and livelihoods at risk throughout the region.
Iran said the Strait of Hormuz, crucial to oil and other exports, would be "completely closed” immediately if the US follows up on President Donald Trump's threat to attack its power plants. Trump late Saturday set a 48-hour deadline to open the strait.
Israeli leaders visited one of two southern communities near a secretive nuclear research site struck by Iranian missiles late Saturday, with scores of people wounded. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it was a “miracle” no one was killed.
Netanyahu claimed Israel and the US were well on their way to achieving their war goals. The aims have ranged from weakening Iran's nuclear programme, missile programme and support for armed proxies to enabling the Iranian people to overthrow the theocracy.
There has been no sign of an uprising, nor of an end to the fighting that has shaken the global economy, sent oil prices surging and endangered some of the world's busiest air corridors. The war, which the US and Israel launched February 28, has killed over 2,000 people.
The Iranian-backed Hezbollah claimed responsibility for an airstrike that killed a man in northern Israel, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called Israel's new targeting of bridges in the south “a prelude to a ground invasion.”
India pays Iran’s Strait of Hormuz fee for oil tanker to pass.
— Radar 𝘸 Archie🚨 (@RadarHits) March 22, 2026
Nations paying for oil in Yuan are granted safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
Donald Trump has achieved the Petro-Yuan, and undermined the U.S. hegemony through the petro-dollar. pic.twitter.com/TghcwelDp1
“More weeks of fighting against Iran and Hezbollah are expected for us,” said Israeli military spokesman Brig. Gen. Effie Defrin.
Energy and desalination plants are threatened
Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz that connects the Persian Gulf to the rest of the world, while claiming safe passage for vessels from countries other than its enemies. Roughly one-fifth of global oil supply passes through it, but attacks on ships have stopped nearly all tanker traffic.
Trump said if Iran didn't open the strait, the US would destroy its “various POWER PLANTS, STARTING WITH THE BIGGEST ONE FIRST!”
The US has argued that Iran's Revolutionary Guard controls much of the country's infrastructure and uses it to power the war effort. Under international law, power plants that benefit civilians can be targeted only if the military advantage outweighs the suffering it causes them, legal scholars say.
Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf responded on X that if Iran's power plants and infrastructure are targeted, then vital infrastructure across the region -- including energy and desalination facilities critical for drinking water in Gulf nations -- would be considered legitimate targets and “irreversibly destroyed.”
Qalibaf later added that “entities that finance the US military budget are legitimate targets."
Attacks on power plants would be “inherently indiscriminate and clearly disproportionate" and a war crime, Iran's UN ambassador wrote to the Security Council, according to the state-run IRNA news agency.
Strikes in Israel and Iran bring new nuclear concerns
Iran said its strikes in the Negev Desert late Saturday were in retaliation for the latest attack on Iran's main nuclear enrichment site in Natanz, according to state-run media.
Tehran praised its attack as a show of strength, even as Israel's military asserts that Iranian missile launches have decreased since the war began.
Southern Israel's main hospital received at least 175 wounded from Arad and Dimona, deputy director Roy Kessous told The Associated Press.
Israel is widely believed to possess nuclear weapons, though it doesn't confirm or deny their existence.
Israel denied responsibility for hitting Natanz on Saturday. The Pentagon declined to comment on the strike.

The International Atomic Energy Agency has said the bulk of Iran's estimated 441 kg of enriched uranium -- the issue at the heart of tensions -- is elsewhere, beneath the rubble at its Isfahan facility.

sources.news_title: Trump’s Ultimatum Comes Back to Bite Him as Enemy Issues New Threat
sources.text:
President Donald Trump’s deafening ultimatum to Iran looks like a failure.
On Saturday night, the 79-year-old commander-in-chief threatened to “destroy” Iran’s power plants if Iran did not end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours.
Tehran’s reply came earlier, but it was not the concession Trump had hoped for.
Iran’s parliament speaker Mohammad Bakr Qalibaf warned on Sunday that Iran would “irreversibly” destroy its Middle Eastern neighbors’ critical infrastructure, including energy and oil facilities, if Trump follows through on his threat to attack the country’s power grid, Reuters reported.
Qalibaf said such attacks would keep oil prices high for a long time.
Trump is already struggling to contain the economic fallout from the war he launched more than three weeks ago. U.S. natural gas prices surged about 30% as Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait of Hormuz is a vital waterway that carries as much as a fifth of the world’s oil supplies.
Trump appeared to have issued an ultimatum to force Iran to withdraw from the strait, but this appeared to have the opposite effect.
Iran’s powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has warned that it will block the strait if the United States targets its power infrastructure.
“The Strait of Hormuz will be completely closed and will not open until our destroyed power plants are rebuilt,” the Guard said in a statement, according to Reuters.
The possibility of tit-for-tat attacks on civilian infrastructure could further disrupt global markets and heighten concerns that U.S. allies in the Middle East will be drawn deeper into the conflict.
An attack on critical infrastructure would be devastating for Iran’s Gulf neighbors, which use far more electricity per capita than Iran and whose booming desert cities rely heavily on energy-intensive desalination plants for nearly all their drinking water.
Trump’s ultimatum was confusing from the start, coming just an hour after he claimed that the United States was “blowing Iran off the map” and that the country had “no defense” and wanted to “make a deal.” “I don’t!” he said.
The escalation also raised legal red flags, as attacks on civilian infrastructure such as power plants can be considered war crimes under international law.
The Geneva Conventions prohibit attacks on “objects indispensable to the survival of civilians.”
Trump has repeatedly claimed that the United States is “very close” to achieving his evolving war goals, even as thousands of troops are deployed to the region and attacks continue to escalate. The war has killed 13 U.S. service members and more than 1,000 Iranian civilians.
The Daily Beast has reached out to the White House for comment.

sources.news_title: Diesel, gasoline, water, and fertilizer are critically impacted by the supply crunch in the Iran war.
sources.text:
The Energy News Beat Stand Up, and we cover President Trump’s 48 Hour warning to smack down on Iran.
This is a massive supply collapse happening right in front of us, and it has global implications for disasters.
With President Trump dropping the 48-hour smackdown warning to Iran, it brings up a lot of related problems and issues that I go through. Everything from timing, price increases, and why there is potential for the oil rubberband price snap-up.
1. Global Supply Chain Disruptions
The transcript addresses critical shortages affecting multiple sectors—diesel, water, and fertilizer markets—with particular emphasis on how these disruptions are impacting farmers and the broader agricultural sector.
2. Geopolitical Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz
A significant focus on escalating tensions involving President Trump’s ultimatum to Iran, demanding full opening of the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours, with threats to strike Iran’s power plants. This represents a major geopolitical flashpoint.
3. Global Oil & Gas Market Disruptions
Discussion of potential disruptions to crude oil supply from Iran and Iraq, with analysis of how these geopolitical events could affect global oil and gas prices and availability.
4. Divergence Between Paper and Physical Oil Prices
The transcript highlights an important market phenomenon—the gap between paper oil prices and physical crude prices in Asian markets—with concerns about potential significant price spikes.
5. LNG Market Impact
Coverage of Qatar Energy’s force majeure declaration on LNG contracts and its ripple effects on the global LNG market, including opportunities for increased US LNG exports.
6. Regional Energy Crises
Analysis of energy challenges in California and New York, including California’s dependence on imported energy and New York’s aggressive green policies and their negative economic impacts.
7. Alaska Oil & Gas Development
Discussion of recent bids and lease awards in the National Petroleum Reserve Alaska, with investment analysis.
8. Energy Sector Investment Analysis
Review and recommendations regarding various energy company stocks and investment opportunities.
Asian Refiners Scramble: Record Premiums Signal Broader Diesel Strain
Half a world away, the same forces are driving Asian refiners to pay eye-watering premiums for alternative crude. According to OilPrice.com (March 20, 2026), grades from Norway’s Johan Sverdrup field are fetching $11.30 per barrel over Dated Brent, while U.S. Mars crude has swung from a discount to a record $11 premium (now around $6). Southeast Asian barrels like Malaysia’s Labuan and Indonesia’s Minas are commanding over $10 premiums—historically just $2.
Why? Gulf supplies—optimized for many Asian refineries—are curtailed or stuck behind the blocked Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing conflict. Refiners in Japan, Thailand, South Korea, and China are turning to Atlantic Basin and U.S. barrels despite sky-high freight costs and longer voyages. High “crack” spreads (fuel prices over crude) are keeping refiners profitable for now, but the scramble signals tightening diesel and jet fuel markets across Asia.
Thailand has already spent millions daily subsidizing diesel prices and urged calm to avoid hoarding. India, China, and others are prioritizing domestic needs, with some Asian suppliers reportedly deprioritizing distant markets like Australia.
This impacts California right in the consumer pocketbook as they import 40% to 50% of diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel, and just think of the 6 of the remaining 7 refineries are set to close.
Fertilizer Markets Under Siege: A Direct Threat to Global Food Production
Fertilizer prices have surged 35% or more since late February, with urea jumping over 50% in some benchmarks (e.g., from ~$482 to $720 per tonne fob Egypt). The Persian Gulf supplies roughly 30-49% of global urea and ammonia exports, plus major shares of phosphates and sulfur—all routed through the now-paralyzed Strait of Hormuz.
Plants in Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and beyond have curtailed output due to gas supply hits and shipping halts. China has restricted exports until August 2026 to protect domestic farmers. The timing couldn’t be worse: Northern Hemisphere spring planting is underway, and Southern Hemisphere seasons (including Australia’s) are critical.
Mapping the World’s Hot Spots
Australia & Oceania: Immediate diesel shortages and fertilizer shortfalls threaten planting. Regional and agricultural users hit hardest; panic buying already reported.
Asia-Pacific (China, India, Japan, Korea, Thailand, Philippines): Heaviest exposure. 80%+ of Middle East crude/LNG heads here; fertilizer dependence is acute (India sources 40%+ urea from Gulf). Rationing risks, higher input costs, and manufacturing slowdowns loom.
Europe: Diesel and jet fuel shortfalls (Gulf supplied up to 60% of some European jet fuel pre-crisis). Low gas stocks exacerbate fertilizer production woes.
United States & North America: Rising diesel (~$3.90–$5+/gallon in places) and fertilizer costs squeeze farm margins ahead of planting. Less import-dependent but still vulnerable to global price spikes.
Developing Regions (Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Latin America): Highest food-security risk. Higher farm costs + remittance losses could spike hunger and inflation where margins are thinnest.
Middle East/Gulf: Ground zero—desalination plants (energy-intensive and reliant on disrupted gas/power) face collateral risks, potentially compounding local water stress.
Water enters the equation indirectly but critically: Gulf desalination (supplying 42-90% of local freshwater) depends on the same energy infrastructure now under strain, while higher diesel prices inflate irrigation pumping costs worldwide.
Consumer Impacts: From Farm Gate to Dinner Plate
Expect:Higher fuel prices at the pump—diesel spikes already feeding into trucking, shipping, and freight surcharges.
Rising grocery bills as fertilizer and diesel costs push up crop production expenses. Corn, wheat, and staples will feel it first; analysts warn of renewed food inflation after a brief lull.
Potential shortages or rationing in vulnerable markets will hit low-income households hardest.
Broader economic drag: Transport, mining, and manufacturing slowdowns could slow growth and employment.
The message is clear: diesel powers the tractors, trucks, and ships; fertilizer feeds the crops; and water ties it all together through energy-intensive systems. Disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz have exposed just how interconnected—and fragile—these supply chains truly are.
This should also be considered a reaffirmation that we were never in an energy transition, as wind and solar could not even begin to supply the global energy supply of transportation, agriculture, and manufacturing.
We have about 12 hours left in the 28 hours, but we are on Trump time, so we do not know when that may happen. If President Trump does take out the Iranian power plants, it will cause some huge problems that people are not talking about. If we take Kharg Island and implement the Venezuelan-style controls through the Bank of Qatar, we will see peace, but whether the Iranian RGC blows up things on the way out is a huge question.
If we take out the Iranian grid, it may take out Iraq as they get 60% of their power from Iran. Between them, that is an estimated 5 million barrels of oil per day that may be delayed back onto the market. Now add into the other fields that have been hit, and my crayon of spare capacity is drawing a pretty thin line of supply once the 200 million barrels of oil on the water are used. That is about a 2.5-week supply in the market.
Calculated Differences (March 2026):
Brent vs. WTI (paper spread): +$14.00/bbl (Brent premium; widened dramatically from historical ~$4–7 norms).
Dubai vs. Brent (paper-to-physical Asia): +$25.63/bbl.
Murban vs. Brent: +$34.21/bbl.
OPEC Basket vs. Brent: +$22.87/bbl.
These are not minor quality tweaks—they reflect a broken market where physical supply constraints (especially in the Middle East) have sent real delivered costs soaring while paper futures lag. U.S. refiner acquisition costs (EIA composite) remain lower in lagged monthly data (~$61/bbl as of January 2026 pre-surge), but current spot physical deals for imported and domestic grades are rapidly converging toward higher delivered realities as arbitrage and exports adjust.
The “Snap” Potential: Why Paper Prices Could Surge Violently Upward
The current paper-physical disconnect is unsustainable. Physical markets lead during real supply stress because refineries must secure actual barrels or shut down. Paper markets, dominated by financial speculators and hedgers, can lag until forced to converge via arbitrage, rolling futures, or forced buying.A “snap” upward in paper prices (Brent/WTI futures jumping $20–$50+ in weeks) is highly plausible if the current drivers persist. Recent history shows exactly this dynamic: physical Dubai premiums exploded to $37–$50 over futures post-conflict escalation, with paper only partially catching up.
Triggers for a Huge Paper Price Spike:
Prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption (20% of global oil flows)—Iran-related conflict has already choked shipping, driving physical premiums to record levels.
Escalating Middle East outages (Iran strikes, tanker insurance spikes, rerouting costs).
Asian demand surge or SPR releases failing to bridge the physical gap.
Speculative short-covering in futures as physical tightness forces refiners to bid up benchmarks.
If the Strait reopens quickly or massive SPR dumps succeed, the snap could reverse downward. But current signals point to upward risk for paper: European physicals and sour crudes are already at all-time highs, pulling futures along.
What This Means for Consumers
Refineries pass higher delivered costs straight into pump prices. Gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel crack spreads are widening rapidly. Expect U.S. average gasoline to climb toward $4–$5+/gallon (or higher regionally) if paper snaps up another $20–$30. Households, airlines, and trucking fleets face immediate pain—higher inflation, squeezed budgets, and potential supply shortages at the pump. The lag is short: physical costs hit refiners within days to weeks.
What This Means for Investors
This is a generational opportunity in energy. Investors in paper oil (futures, USO, BNO ETFs, or Brent-linked products) stand to capture explosive upside as benchmarks converge upward to physical reality. Oil majors (Exxon, Chevron), midstream, and refiners with locked-in physical margins could see windfall profits. Energy stocks and high-yield E&P plays may rerate sharply.
Conversely, those short paper or exposed to consumer-facing sectors (airlines, autos) face downside. The key: monitor physical differentials daily—when Dubai/Murban premiums compress back toward Brent, the snap is over. Position sizing, hedging with options, and watching Strait of Hormuz news flow are critical. In a snap scenario, paper oil could deliver 20–50%+ returns in months for leveraged or futures-based investors—far outpacing broad equities.
This will take years to recover. I will have more in future articles on this, and it should not have happened.
